Actions available: turn left, turn right, go forward.

raw_output:
<think>
Let me find a path on this 5x5 grid.
Starting position is (4, 0), facing north. The goal is at (0, 1). There is 1 wall tile i must avoid: (3,3).
I'll test turn left, turn right, and go forward at each decision point and pick the best.
Taking turn left puts me at (4,0) facing west — leaving 5 step(s) to go. Taking turn right puts me at (4,0) facing east — leaving 5 step(s) to go. Taking go forward puts me at (3,0) facing north — leaving 4 step(s) to go. Going with go forward for now — 4 more step(s) to the goal.
go forward -> turn left leads to (3,0) facing west — 4 step(s) remaining. go forward -> turn right leads to (3,0) facing east — 4 step(s) remaining. go forward -> go forward leads to (2,0) facing north — 3 step(s) remaining. go forward -> go forward looks best — only 3 step(s) from the goal.
<grid_token>
(Grid snapshot: currently at (2,0) facing north, 3 step(s) left. Surroundings are clear. Proceeding.)
Following go forward -> go forward -> turn left I'd be at (2,0) facing west — with 3 step(s) still ahead. Following go forward -> go forward -> turn right I'd be at (2,0) facing east — with 3 step(s) still ahead. Following go forward -> go forward -> go forward I'd be at (1,0) facing north — with 2 step(s) still ahead. I'll continue with go forward -> go forward -> go forward; it's the closest, with 2 step(s) to go.
Going go forward -> go forward -> go forward -> turn left brings me to (1,0) facing west — 2 move(s) short of the goal. Going go forward -> go forward -> go forward -> turn right brings me to (1,0) facing east — 2 move(s) short of the goal. Going go forward -> go forward -> go forward -> go forward brings me to (0,0) facing north — 1 move(s) short of the goal. go forward -> go forward -> go forward -> go forward gets me the furthest, leaving just 1 step(s). I'll keep this.
<grid_token>
(Visual check: I'm at (0,0) facing north, 1 step(s) from goal. Path ahead looks clear. Continuing.)
If I take go forward -> go forward -> go forward -> go forward -> turn left, I land at (0,0) facing west — still 1 step(s) from the goal. If I take go forward -> go forward -> go forward -> go forward -> turn right, I land at (0,0) facing east — still 1 step(s) from the goal. If I take go forward -> go forward -> go forward -> go forward -> go forward, I land at (0,0) facing north — but the way is blocked — not an option. Going with go forward -> go forward -> go forward -> go forward -> turn right for now — 1 more step(s) to the goal.
Taking go forward -> go forward -> go forward -> go forward -> turn right -> turn left puts me at (0,0) facing north — leaving 1 step(s) to go. Taking go forward -> go forward -> go forward -> go forward -> turn right -> turn right puts me at (0,0) facing south — leaving 1 step(s) to go. Taking go forward -> go forward -> go forward -> go forward -> turn right -> go forward puts me at (0,1) facing east — which is exactly the goal. go forward -> go forward -> go forward -> go forward -> turn right -> go forward gets me to the goal, so that's my pick.
<grid_token>
(Checking the grid: position (0,1) facing east, distance to goal = 0. No walls nearby — safe to continue. Moving on.)
</think>

Let me find a path on this 5x5 grid.
Starting position is (0, 4), facing south. The goal is at (1, 0). There are 3 wall tiles i must avoid: (0,0), (2,2), (2,4).
I'll test turn left, turn right, and go forward at each decision point and pick the best.
Following turn left I'd be at (0,4) facing east — with 5 step(s) still ahead. Following turn right I'd be at (0,4) facing west — with 5 step(s) still ahead. Following go forward I'd be at (1,4) facing south — with 4 step(s) still ahead. Going with go forward for now — 4 more step(s) to the goal.
Going go forward -> turn left brings me to (1,4) facing east — 4 move(s) short of the goal. Going go forward -> turn right brings me to (1,4) facing west — 4 move(s) short of the goal. Going go forward -> go forward brings me to (1,4) facing south — — blocked by a wall, so no. go forward -> turn right looks best — only 4 step(s) from the goal.
<grid_token>
(Checking the grid: position (1,4) facing west, distance to goal = 4. Careful — nearby wall(s) at [(2, 4)]. Moving on.)
If I take go forward -> turn right -> turn left, I land at (1,4) facing south — still 4 step(s) from the goal. If I take go forward -> turn right -> turn right, I land at (1,4) facing north — still 4 step(s) from the goal. If I take go forward -> turn right -> go forward, I land at (1,3) facing west — still 3 step(s) from the goal. I'll continue with go forward -> turn right -> go forward; it's the closest, with 3 step(s) to go.
Taking go forward -> turn right -> go forward -> turn left puts me at (1,3) facing south — leaving 3 step(s) to go. Taking go forward -> turn right -> go forward -> turn right puts me at (1,3) facing north — leaving 3 step(s) to go. Taking go forward -> turn right -> go forward -> go forward puts me at (1,2) facing west — leaving 2 step(s) to go. go forward -> turn right -> go forward -> go forward gets me the furthest, leaving just 2 step(s). I'll keep this.
<grid_token>
(Grid snapshot: currently at (1,2) facing west, 2 step(s) left. Note: wall(s) next to me at [(2, 2)]. Proceeding.)
go forward -> turn right -> go forward -> go forward -> turn left leads to (1,2) facing south — 2 step(s) remaining. go forward -> turn right -> go forward -> go forward -> turn right leads to (1,2) facing north — 2 step(s) remaining. go forward -> turn right -> go forward -> go forward -> go forward leads to (1,1) facing west — 1 step(s) remaining. Going with go forward -> turn right -> go forward -> go forward -> go forward for now — 1 more step(s) to the goal.
Following go forward -> turn right -> go forward -> go forward -> go forward -> turn left I'd be at (1,1) facing south — with 1 step(s) still ahead. Following go forward -> turn right -> go forward -> go forward -> go forward -> turn right I'd be at (1,1) facing north — with 1 step(s) still ahead. Following go forward -> turn right -> go forward -> go forward -> go forward -> go forward I'd be at (1,0) facing west — which means I've reached the goal. I'll go with go forward -> turn right -> go forward -> go forward -> go forward -> go forward — it reaches the goal.
<grid_token>
(Visual check: I'm at (1,0) facing west, 0 step(s) from goal. Watch out — wall(s) adjacent at [(0, 0)]. Continuing.)
